thread:
alex: FYI i'm onboarding Kite7B (7B, transformer-xl style rotary) into the int4 pipeline. quick smoke shows repeating tokens after ~2048 tokens when using our usual quant recipe. looks like kv-cache replay/shift?

sasha: can you paste the minimal repro? :thinking:

alex: repro steps:
```bash
export MODEL=kite7b-fp16
python serve_local.py --model $MODEL --quant int4 --seed 42 --max-tokens 4096 
# prompt: 1..100 repeated then a question
```
output snippet (after token 2048):
```
... token_2047 token_2048 token_2049 token_2050
token_2051 token_2052 token_2053 token_2054
>>> token_2055 token_2055 token_2055 token_2055
```

lina: hmm repeating token looks like either rotary misalignment (headmap) or kv cache index wrap. did you try running fp16 baseline with same prompt?

alex: yes fp16 baseline is clean. diff between fp16 and int4 shows logits diverge around token 2047 then collapse to a high-prob token.

ben: what quant backend? we have a newer kernel change that folded head dims for layout 'headmajor' recently. if Kite's weights exported with 'headminor' ordering we might be misinterpreting rotary dims.

alex: using our nightly quant tool (quantize v0.9.1) with --layout headmajor. model originally exported from convert_tools as layout=headminor. i tried swapping layout flag and re-quant but still saw drift, though collapse point shifted a bit.

sasha: can you run a quick check: compare rotary angles between fp16 and quantized converted model? something like:
```py
# quick check
angles_fp16 = load_angles('kite7b-fp16')\nangles_int4 = load_angles('kite7b-int4')\nprint((angles_fp16 - angles_int4).abs().max())\n```

alex: running now, attaching tiny log: "max diff = 0.00012"

lina: tiny diff so probably not angle truncation. have you inspected token->id mapping? sometimes exports add sentinel tokens or shift vocab indexes which can cause kv misalignment when we assume same BOS/EOS indices.

alex: good point. i compared tokenizer.vocab size and top tokens: fp16 vocab_size=50256, converted=50258. two extra tokens at the tail. when i remapped using our vocab-normalizer and re-exported to the same indices the collapse moved to ~3072 instead of 2048.

ben: that suggests a token-id shift interacting with KV positions. likely we have code that caches positions by token id in some edge case. can you grep for any token-id-based cache indexing in runtime? search for kv_cache[token_id] or similar.

alex: found one spot in runtime/sessions/kv_cache.py: index = token_id % self.slot_count  # legacy sharding; added in 2021, never hit big longctx models.

sasha: oof. that mod-based sharding explains periodic repeats when token ids offset. we should not use token_id for cache slot; should use absolute sequence index. filing a small PR to revert. @triagebot please create an oncall task and assign to eng-runtime.

triagebot: Created task #ENGRT-1123 "kv_cache: stop using token_id mod for slot index (kite7b int4 longctx repeat)" and assigned to @ben and @alex. Priority: P2. Link: https://tasks.redwood/in/ENGRT-1123

lina: meanwhile, let's add a regression test: generate a repeating numeric prompt of length 8192 and assert no token repeat collapse for both fp16 and int4. also run our eval harness to compare perplexity and exact-match on a small qa set.

alex: will add tests and run nightly int4 benchmark; i also want to try running quantize with --preserve_vocab_indices to avoid conversion anomalies.

ben: nice triage. once PR lands, rerun the full onnx->quant pipeline and do a bitwise head-dim sanity check (head ordering). i can help with perf runs.

sasha: thanks team. keep notes in the kite7b onboarding doc and ping #eng-runtime when you have PR. :thumbsup:
